messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm planning a dead-man switch + routing-override for the precision toggle rollout tomorrow. Need quick thumbs on guardrail thresholds and who gets paged if the dead-man fires. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4321. Plan: staged canaries 0.5% -> 2% -> 10%. Key metrics: 99p latency, p50 token cost, user-visible error rate. Abort if thresholds exceeded.

ryan: LGTM on approach. For routing-override, prefer fallback to fp16 in-region. If capacity constrained, route to dedicated pool not hosted fallback. Do we have spare capacity for that path? cc @oliver

zara: Quick concrete thresholds proposal: 99p latency > 1.5x baseline OR 5xx rate > 0.2% OR user-visible errors > 0.1% -> abort/rollback. Add quality guard: eval drop (rouge/QA) > 1.5% -> abort. Thoughts?

oliver: +1 to those thresholds. Also add an automated circuit-breaker that flips the feature flag off, posts to #incidents and triggers the oncall pager. I can own the alert rule. Who should be the pager target?

maya: I added config fields in the PR:
```json
{
  "flag": "quant_precision_toggle",
  "stages": [0.005, 0.02, 0.1],
  "deadman": {
    "enabled": true,
    "latency_mult": 1.5,
    "error_rate": 0.001,
    "eval_drop_pct": 1.5
  },
  "routing": {
    "fallback": "fp16",
    "overflow_pool": "dedicated-gpu"
  }
}
```
(Names are draft — happy to iterate)

ryan: :eyes: PR touches route selection. If we route to dedicated pool we need to ensure autoscale headroom. I'll check headroom and update PR with a capacity guard. Also pinging infra on-call to confirm.

zara: Please add telemetry tags `quant_rollout.stage` and `quant_rollout.reason` (e.g. "manual", "deadman") so we can query rollback causes in the postmortem.

oliver: I'll own the alert + runbook. Plan: mute for 15m after flip to avoid noise, then escalate to pager if not resolved. Pager target: infra-oncall first, then eng-sre.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: deploy started for pr-4321 -> staging (sha abc123)

maya: Thanks. @ryan can you do a quick safety review of the route selection change? @zara can you confirm the canary eval harness can run on live 0.5% traffic and push the job? I'll hold the flip until both thumbs.

ryan: On it. I will review the route selection diff and the capacity guard within the next hour.

zara: I scheduled the canary eval now (runs during first window). I'll post results to the thread and add a quick dashboard for the eval metrics.

maya: Final scheduling: rollout window 10:00-14:00 PT tomorrow. Abort/rollback windows: for stage1 10:30-10:45, stage2 11:30-11:45. I'll post an ops note to #incidents right before the flip. :thumbsup:

oliver: :thumbsup: Created alert `quant_rollout_deadman` and linked pager + runbook (summary: flip flag off, notify #incidents, run immediate traffic dump).

maya: Great — thanks everyone. If anyone spots a missing check or a blocker in the PR ping me. Otherwise I'll proceed with the flip plan tomorrow.
